for-unto-us-a-child-is-born.sources: // Sources: the song file (the parts' guide notes, as reviewed 2026-11-18), tools: ~/Code/arranger-keep/partfacts.py; licence.source: Handel, The Messiah, ed. Ebenezer Prout, full score (London: Novello, copyright 1902), No. 12, Handel's own four voice parts, the orchestra left out; in Handel's key, G, as printed

parts.soprano: Starts the chorus alone with Handel's tune, "For unto us a Child is born", and has the first long run on "born". Sings most often on D, then C, A and B, up to its top A only once, a quick note at the top of that first run on "born", and down to its low E only on "us" and "a" in its first "unto us a Son is given".
parts.alto: Comes in third with the tune, in the key of the dominant, and runs in thirds under the soprano on the last "born". Sings most often on G, then F-sharp and A, up to its top C only on "His" in its second "be upon His shoulder" and on two quick notes of its last run on "born", and down to its low A only at the end of that same "shoulder": the last note of "shoul-" and "der,".
parts.tenor: Comes in second with the tune, an octave under the soprano. Sings most often on D, then E and C, up to its top G on "His" in its first "be upon His shoulder" and its first "and His Name", on "E-" and "ver-" of its first "Everlasting", on "Name" in its second "and His Name", on "Won-" and "Coun-" in the second and the last "Wonderful, Counsellor", on the held end of "shoul-" in its second "shoulder", on "us" in the middle one of its last three "unto us a Son is given", and on "His" and "be" in the last "and His Name shall be called"; and down to its low E only on "us" and "a" in its first "unto us a Son is given".
parts.bass: Comes in last with the tune, an octave under the alto, and leaps an octave on the first and third "Wonderful, Counsellor". Sings most often on G, then D and C, up to its top E only at the top of its first run on "born" and on "un-" of the "unto us" just after it, and down to its low G only on the last word, "Peace.".

parts_es.soprano: Empieza el coro sola con la melodía de Handel, "For unto us a Child is born", y tiene la primera escala larga sobre "born". Canta con más frecuencia en el Re, luego en el Do, el La y el Si, sube a su La agudo una sola vez, una nota rápida en lo más alto de esa primera escala sobre "born", y baja a su Mi grave solo en "us" y "a" de su primer "unto us a Son is given".
parts_es.alto: Entra en tercer lugar con la melodía, en el tono de la dominante, y corre en terceras por debajo de la soprano en el último "born". Canta con más frecuencia en el Sol, luego en el Fa sostenido y el La, sube a su Do agudo solo en "His" de su segundo "be upon His shoulder" y en dos notas rápidas de su última escala sobre "born", y baja a su La grave solo al final de ese mismo "shoulder": la última nota de "shoul-" y "der,".
parts_es.tenor: Entra en segundo lugar con la melodía, una octava por debajo de la soprano. Canta con más frecuencia en el Re, luego en el Mi y el Do, sube a su Sol agudo en "His" de su primer "be upon His shoulder" y de su primer "and His Name", en "E-" y "ver-" de su primer "Everlasting", en "Name" de su segundo "and His Name", en "Won-" y "Coun-" del segundo y el último "Wonderful, Counsellor", en el final sostenido de "shoul-" en su segundo "shoulder", en "us" del segundo de sus tres últimos "unto us a Son is given" y en "His" y "be" del último "and His Name shall be called"; y baja a su Mi grave solo en "us" y "a" de su primer "unto us a Son is given".
parts_es.bass: Entra en último lugar con la melodía, una octava por debajo de la contralto, y salta una octava en el primer y el tercer "Wonderful, Counsellor". Canta con más frecuencia en el Sol, luego en el Re y el Do, sube a su Mi agudo solo en lo más alto de su primera escala sobre "born" y en "un-" del "unto us" que la sigue, y baja a su Sol grave solo en la última palabra, "Peace.".
